sentences.text:
Against an award dated 31.07.2012 passed under Section 26 of the Jammu and Kashmir Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990 (in short, Act of 1990) by the reference court of learned District Judge,
Kishtwar, the Indenting Department i.e., Union of India, acting through its Officer Commanding 118, RCC (GREF) came forward with a time barred statutory appeal filed on 28.12.2012 under Section 52 of the Act of 1990.

entities.text: Jammu and Kashmir Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Since the appeal was suffering delay of 56 days, the delay came to be condoned in terms of an order dated 18.12.2020 resulting in taking on record the statutory appeal of the appellant-Union of India against an award dated 31.07.2012 on file No. 9/Civil Reference by the reference court of learned District Judge, Kishtwar.

sentences.text:
The Collector's awarded compensation of an amount of Rs. 2,34,025/- came to be enhanced by the reference court of learned District Judge, Kishtwar to an amount of Rs. 3,11,476/- with respect to the respondent No. 1 and an amount of Rs. 1,55,001/- from an amount of Rs. 69,000/-
4.

The land acquisition proceedings with respect to the respective immovable properties of the respondents came to be set into effect by the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate),
Kishtwar for the purpose of acquisition of land measuring 218.14 kanals situated in village Bhagna,
tehsil Kishtwar for the purpose of road alignment for widening of Galhar-Sansari road.

entities.text:
Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate),
Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. In the land measuring 218.14 kanals coming under acquisition, the respondent No. 1-Chuni Lal Parihar's property in the form of one house and one shop and the respondent Jo. 2-Girdhari Lal's property in the form of one shop situated in village Hidyal had also fallen under acquisition.

6. At no point of time during the course of acquisition, the respondents stood individually notified about the acquisition process and as such remained unaware of the acquisition which resulted in passing of a land acquisition award No. 84-89/SDMK dated 06.04.1999.
7.

Upon coming to have the knowledge of the issuance of the said award dated 06.04.1999, the respondents No. 1 and 2, in their individual capacity, had approached the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar whereupon they came to receive the compensation assessed in terms of the said award on 07.05.2002 and 23.05.2002 respectively under protest.

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. The respondents No. 1 and 2 acting independently came forward with their respective applications dated 02.09.2002 and 16.10.2001 addressed to the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar seeking reference of the matter for determination of the court with respect to the quantum of compensation.

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. Being dissatisfied with the quantum assessed by the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar, the two applications were made by the respondents within a period of six months from the date of their respective receipt of the compensation awarded in terms of the land acquisition award dated 06.04.1999.

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 10. The Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar came to entertain the applications so filed by the respondents No. 1 and 2 and made a reference under Section 18 of the Act of 1990 vide reference No. 491/LA dated 08.01.2003 which came to be taken on file No. 9/Civil Reference dated 04.02.2003.

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In his reference No. 491/LA dated 08.01.2003, the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar nowhere observed or held that the applications filed by the respondents for seeking reference was barred under law in terms of proviso to Section 18 of the Act of 1990.

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
11. The respondents exercised their right for seeking reference by reference to Clause-(b) to proviso to sub section 2 of Section 18 of the Act of 1990 by a position that neither they were present nor represented before the Collector at the time when he had made his award so as to have the run of the time against them for seeking reference within a period of six weeks and submitted that they were Uoi Through vs Chuni Lal Parihar on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22464065/
2 unaware of the issuance of the land acquisition award and further that no exercise as envisaged under sub section 12 of the Act of 1990 had been undertaken at the end of the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar for the sake of setting the time to run against the respondents for the purpose of seeking the reference.

entities.text: Uoi Through vs Chuni Lal Parihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In the reference proceedings, the appellant herein contested the reference by raising no objection whatsoever relatable to the time barred reference.

13. The reference court in terms of an order dated 18.04.2009 came to frame the issues in the reference proceedings which are as under:
(i) Whether the compensation in respect of one house and one shop owned by Chuni Lal Parihar applicant No. 1 and one shop owned by father of Girdhari Lal application No. 2, acquired for widening of Galhar-Sansari road has not been assessed properly i.e as per marked value existing in the area, if so what is its market value?
OPP (ii) Relief.

14. In the present memo of appeal, the appellant is impugning the reference award passed by the learned District Judge, Kishtwar on the plea that the reference was time barred and this issue ought to have been considered by the reference court.

15. This Court cannot lend any acceptance to this objection of the appellant in the present appeal given the fact that no such insistence was made by the appellant before the reference court otherwise an issue to the said effect would have been definitely struck by the reference court.

Even if such a plea would have been taken by the appellant with respect to the time barred reference even in that scenario that would have been rejected for the simple reason that the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar in his reference at no point of time ever put it on record that the respondents have come late in seeking the reference against the award dated 31.07.2012 on account of the fact that the filing of the award under Section 12 of the Land Acquisition Act Svt. 1990 had not been carried out at the end of the Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition (Sub Divisional Magistrate), Kishtwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
16. Mr. L.K. Sharma, learned Senior Advocate has referred to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as "Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh Vs. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer"
reported in 1961 AIR (SC) 1500 and of this Court in case titled as "Haji Gh. Rasool Kitab Vs.
Collector" reported in 1991 KLJ 106 to support the reference as being within time.

entities.text:
Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh Vs. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer"
reported in 1961 AIR (SC) 1500
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Haji Gh. Rasool Kitab Vs.
Collector" reported in 1991 KLJ 106
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said two judgments apply on all fours in the context of the present case.

17. With respect to the quantum of compensation enhanced by the reference court, the appellant is making a very feeble reference in its memo of appeal that the enhancement of the compensation, as accorded by the reference Court, is exorbitant against the prevailing market rate without setting out any instance to mismatch the rate so assessed by the reference court for the purpose of enhancing compensation in favour of the respondents.

entities.text: Uoi Through vs Chuni Lal Parihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the aforesaid, the appeal of the appellant is held to be merit less and is accordingly dismissed along with connected application(s), if any.

19. The appellant is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with interest component and along with all the attending entitlement before the reference court within a period of three months from today.

In case if any amount came to be deposited by the appellant in connection with the present appeal, pursuant to any direction passed by this Court, then the said amount shall be remitted back by the Registry to the Reference Court of learned District Judge, Kishtwar.
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 10.05.2024
